breakfast.name: Fufu and Peanut Soup
instructions: Make fufu: boil and pound yam
Cook peanut soup with chicken and vegetables
Serve fufu balls with soup

breakfast.name: Akpan (Fermented Corn Yogurt)
instructions: Mix corn dough with water
Strain
Sweeten and serve cold

breakfast.name: Akpan (Fermented Corn Porridge)
ingredients: Fermented corn dough (akpan -- prepared in advance by fermenting cornmeal in water for 2 days)
instructions: Akpan is the Togolese fermented corn porridge -- a Fon and Ewe staple breakfast
The corn dough is fermented for 2-3 days until slightly sour
Cooked in boiling water until thickened
Eaten warm with sugar or condensed milk
The fermentation gives a slightly sour, tangy flavor
Sold at roadside stalls in the morning across Togo and Benin
breakfast.description: Togolese fermented corn porridge -- akpan, cornmeal fermented for 2-3 days (slightly sour) cooked into a warm porridge. Eaten with sugar or condensed milk. Sold at roadside stalls in the morning across Togo and Benin.

breakfast.name: Bread with Beans (Pain Haricot)
ingredients: Spiced black-eyed peas or cowpeas (cooked soft with onion and palm oil)
instructions: Pain haricot is the West African French-colonial baguette with beans
French colonization of Togo (1914-1960 under French League of Nations mandate)
The baguette was adopted as the everyday bread
Split baguette filled with spiced beans cooked in palm oil
A quick, filling, cheap breakfast
breakfast.description: Togolese baguette with beans -- French colonial baguette (Togo was under French mandate 1914-1960) split and filled with spiced black-eyed peas cooked in palm oil. A quick, filling street breakfast.

lunch.name: Djenkoumé (Corn and Tomato Paste)
instructions: Cook tomato sauce with crab/fish
Add cornmeal, stir until thick paste forms
Cook 20 min
lunch.description: Thick corn-tomato paste — Togo's national dish.

lunch.name: Akoumé (Corn Paste) with Sauce
instructions: Boil water, stir in cornmeal
Cook until thick
Shape into balls
Serve with sauce

lunch.name: Ablo (Steamed Corn Cakes)
ingredients: Corn dough (fermented -- same base as akpan)
Palm oil sauce or stew (to serve alongside)
instructions: Ablo are the Togolese steamed corn cakes
Fermented corn dough steamed in small cups or molds
Soft, slightly sour, slightly sweet
Eaten alongside stews and soups
The texture: softer and spongier than fufu
lunch.description: Togolese steamed corn cakes -- fermented corn dough steamed in small molds until soft and slightly sour. Eaten alongside stews and soups. Softer and spongier than fufu.

lunch.name: Sauce Arachide (Peanut Sauce with Meat)
instructions: Sauce arachide is the West African peanut stew -- eaten from Senegal to Cameroon to Togo
The peanut paste is the base: rich, nutty, thick
Chicken or meat simmered in the peanut broth
Palm oil for richness and color
Eaten with fufu, rice, or attieke (cassava couscous)
The ubiquitous West African main course
lunch.description: Togolese peanut stew -- ground peanut paste cooked with chicken or meat, tomatoes, and palm oil into a rich, nutty stew. The West African peanut stew that spans from Senegal to Cameroon. Eaten with fufu, rice, or attieke.

lunch.name: Fufu (Yam or Cassava)
instructions: Fufu is the West African pounded starch -- the foundation of the meal
In Togo: yam fufu is preferred in the north; cassava fufu in the south
Yam is pounded in a large mortar with a heavy pestle -- two people traditionally, one pounding, one turning
The pounding motion is rhythmic and requires skill
The fufu becomes smooth, elastic, and slightly sticky
Eaten by pulling off a small piece, making an indentation, and using it to scoop stew
lunch.description: Togolese pounded yam or cassava -- fufu, yam pounded in a large mortar until smooth and elastic (two people traditionally: one pounding, one turning). In Togo, yam fufu is northern; cassava fufu is southern. Eaten by scooping stew.

dinner.name: Gboma Dessi (Spinach Stew)
instructions: Sauté onion and tomatoes in palm oil
Add spinach and fish
Simmer until thick
dinner.description: Spinach stew with palm oil and smoked fish.

dinner.name: Grilled Tilapia
instructions: Score fish, rub with spices
Grill over charcoal
Serve with banku or rice

dinner.name: Gari Foto (Cassava Flour with Eggs)
instructions: Gari foto is the Togolese and Ghanaian cassava flour dish
Gari: dried grated cassava, toasted until it resembles a dry, coarse couscous
Cooked with eggs, tomato, and onion in palm oil
The gari absorbs the oil and egg -- becomes slightly moist and fragrant
A quick, cheap meal made from stored gari
dinner.description: Togolese cassava flour with eggs -- gari (dried toasted cassava couscous-like) cooked with scrambled eggs, tomato, and onion in palm oil. The gari absorbs the oil and becomes fragrant. A quick, pantry-staple meal.

dinner.name: Aloco (Fried Plantain)
ingredients: Chilli sauce or onion-tomato sauce (for serving)
instructions: Aloco are the West African fried ripe plantains
Very ripe plantains (the black-spotted ones): the sugars have developed
Fried in hot oil until caramelized and golden
Eaten with a tomato-onion-chilli sauce
A ubiquitous street food across Francophone West Africa
dinner.description: Togolese fried ripe plantain -- very ripe (black-spotted) plantains fried in hot oil until caramelized. Eaten with a tomato-onion-chilli sauce. Ubiquitous street food across Francophone West Africa.

dinner.name: Tchakpalo (Sorghum Beer Chicken)
ingredients: Tchakpalo (local sorghum beer -- used for marinating and braising)
instructions: Tchakpalo is the Togolese sorghum beer -- and also a cooking medium
The beer is used to marinate and braise chicken
The fermented, slightly sour beer tenderizes the meat
Adds a complex, slightly tangy flavor
A ceremonial and celebratory dish
dinner.description: Togolese sorghum beer chicken -- chicken marinated and braised in tchakpalo (local sorghum beer), the fermented beer tenderizing the meat and adding a tangy, complex flavor. A ceremonial dish.

snacks.name: Koklo Meme (Grilled Chicken)
instructions: Marinate chicken
Grill over charcoal
Serve with piment (chili sauce)
snacks.description: Grilled chicken with chili sauce — Lomé street food.

snacks.name: Beignets de Haricot (Bean Fritters)
ingredients: Black-eyed peas (soaked, peeled, ground to a paste)
instructions: Bean fritters (beignets de haricot) are the West African street snack
Black-eyed peas soaked, peeled, and ground to a smooth paste
Seasoned with onion and chilli
Dropped into hot oil and fried until golden
Eaten as a snack with pepper sauce
Called akara in Nigeria, kosai in Hausa, koose in Ghana -- the same fritter across West Africa
snacks.description: Togolese black-eyed pea fritters -- peeled, ground black-eyed pea paste seasoned with onion and chilli, fried until golden. The same fritter exists across West Africa as akara (Nigeria), koose (Ghana), kosai (Hausa). Eaten with pepper sauce.

snacks.name: Koki (Bean Cake)
instructions: Koki is the steamed bean cake wrapped in banana leaves
Ground black-eyed peas mixed with palm oil and onion
Wrapped tightly in banana leaves
Steamed until firm
Unwrapped to reveal an orange-red cake from the palm oil
Eaten as a snack or as part of a meal
snacks.description: Togolese steamed bean cake -- ground black-eyed peas mixed with palm oil and onion, wrapped in banana leaves and steamed until firm. Unwrapped: an orange-red cake from the palm oil. Eaten as a snack or meal component.

snacks.name: Roasted Corn (Mais Grille)
instructions: Roasted corn is the ubiquitous West African street snack
Whole corn cobs roasted over charcoal
The corn chars slightly on the outside
Eaten by the roadside everywhere across Togo and West Africa
The simplest and most common snack
snacks.description: Togolese roadside roasted corn -- whole corn cobs roasted over charcoal until slightly charred, eaten by the roadside. The simplest and most universal West African street snack.

desserts.name: Fried Plantains with Sugar
instructions: Fry plantains until golden
Sprinkle with sugar

desserts.name: Beignets Souffles (Puff Puff)
ingredients: Flour, yeast, sugar, salt, water, nutmeg
instructions: Puff puff (beignets souffles) are the West African sweet doughnut balls
A simple yeast batter -- more liquid than bread dough
Dropped by spoonfuls into hot oil -- they puff into balls
Lightly sweet and eggy
Eaten as a street dessert or snack -- sold by the bag
Called puff puff in English-speaking West Africa, beignets in Francophone West Africa
desserts.description: Togolese sweet puff puff fritters -- yeast batter dropped into hot oil, puffing into airy sweet balls. Called puff puff (English West Africa) or beignets souffles (Francophone West Africa). Sold by the bag at street stalls.

desserts.name: Pain de Sucre (Sugar Bread)
ingredients: Flour, yeast, sugar, eggs, butter, milk
instructions: Pain de sucre is the sweet enriched bread -- a French-influenced Togolese sweet
An enriched dough with eggs and butter
More cake-like than bread -- slightly sweet
Eaten as a dessert or sweet snack
The French patisserie influence through colonization
desserts.description: Togolese sweet enriched bread -- pain de sucre, an egg-and-butter enriched dough, more cake-like than bread. The French colonial patisserie influence. Eaten as a dessert or afternoon snack.

drinks.name: Tchoukoutou (Millet Beer)
instructions: Cook millet mash
Ferment 3-5 days
Strain

drinks.name: Sodabi (Palm Spirit)
instructions: Distill palm wine in traditional still

drinks.name: Tchoukoutou (Sorghum Beer)
instructions: Tchoukoutou is the traditional Togolese sorghum beer
Malted sorghum fermented over several days
The result is a slightly cloudy, slightly sour, low-alcohol beer
Drunk from communal calabashes
A social and ceremonial drink -- important at funerals, festivals, and celebrations
Made by women in northern Togo
The calabash (gourd cup) is the traditional vessel
drinks.description: Togolese traditional sorghum beer -- tchoukoutou, malted sorghum fermented into a slightly cloudy, mildly sour beer. Drunk from communal calabashes. Made by women in northern Togo. A social and ceremonial drink at funerals, festivals, and celebrations.
